sections.title: Exercise Physiology
sections.intro: Exercise Physiology uses individualised movement and exercise programs to support physical capacity, participation and long-term wellbeing. Programs are designed around the person's current abilities, goals and daily life.

sections.title: Support built around everyday participation.
sections.intro: Therapy goals are individual. These examples show common areas that may be explored when they are relevant to the person and their priorities.

items.title: Strength
items.description: Progressive exercises that build useful strength for daily activities.

items.title: Endurance
items.description: Developing stamina and the ability to stay active for longer.

items.title: Functional capacity
items.description: Improving the physical abilities needed for everyday routines and participation.

items.title: Exercise confidence
items.description: Building comfort, knowledge and confidence around safe physical activity.

items.title: Health-focused movement
items.description: Using structured activity to support general physical wellbeing.

items.title: Sustainable routines
items.description: Creating realistic exercise habits that can fit into everyday life.

panels.title: Goals first, service second.
paragraphs: Programs are individualised and may support adolescents and adults with a variety of functional and wellbeing goals, depending on service suitability.
We start by understanding what is working well, what feels difficult and what meaningful change would look like in daily life. From there, the clinician can recommend a suitable next step.

items.title: Start with your priorities
items.description: Tell us what matters, what is currently difficult and what you hope to change.

items.title: Understand strengths & needs
items.description: Your clinician gathers relevant information and completes assessment where appropriate.

items.title: Build practical strategies
items.description: Sessions focus on meaningful goals and strategies that make sense in real routines.

items.title: Review & adapt
items.description: Progress is reviewed together and the plan is adjusted as needs and goals change.

sections.title: Before you get started.
sections.intro: These answers are general. We can discuss individual circumstances when you contact the team.

items.question: Is Exercise Physiology the same as personal training?
items.answer: Exercise Physiology is an allied health service that uses assessment and tailored exercise programming to address individual health and functional goals.

items.question: Do I need to be fit before I start?
items.answer: No. Programs are designed from your current starting point and progressed at an appropriate pace.

items.question: Can the program focus on everyday function?
items.answer: Yes. Goals can be linked to real tasks, participation, energy and confidence in daily life.

sections.title: Let’s find the right starting point.
